speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)

The classic "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, combined with a subsequent lacy pruritic rash on the extremities and recent viral prodrome, is highly characteristic of Parvovirus B19 infection. No further testing is required to confirm this clinical diagnosis.
